# 2 Samuel Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 187r–188r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_017_page_001.jpg, 2SA_017_page_002.jpg, 2SA_017_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me pick twelve thousand men and set out after David tonight. **2** I'll catch him while he's exhausted and demoralized, and throw him into a panic. All his followers will scatter, and I'll cut down the king — just him, no one else. **3** Then I'll bring everyone back to you. When the man you're after is gone, the whole nation will return in peace."

**4** The plan seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.

**5** But then Absalom said, "Bring in Hushai the Archite as well — let's hear what he thinks."

**6** When Hushai arrived, Absalom told him, "Ahithophel has proposed this plan. Should we follow it? If you have something better, speak up."

**7** Hushai said to Absalom, "For once, Ahithophel's advice is not the right move."

**8** He continued, "You know your father and his men. They are hardened fighters, and right now they are as dangerous as a mother bear whose cubs have been stolen. Your father is a man of war — he won't be sleeping out in the open with the troops.

**9** By now he's already hiding in some cave or ravine. If some of your men fall in the first clash, word will spread: 'Absalom's army has been routed!'

**10** Then even the bravest soldier — a man with the heart of a lion — will lose all courage. For everyone in Israel knows your father is a warrior, and his men are fearless.

**11** Here is what I advise: Gather all Israel to yourself, from Dan to Beersheba — as countless as sand on the shore — and march out personally at their head.

**12** We'll descend on him wherever he is, settling on him like dew on the ground. Not one of his men will survive — not even David himself.

**13** And if he retreats into a city, all Israel will bring ropes and drag the whole place down into the valley until not a single stone is left!"

**14** Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "Hushai's plan is better than Ahithophel's." For the LORD had determined to frustrate Ahithophel's wise counsel, in order to bring disaster on Absalom.

**15** Then Hushai told the priests Zadok and Abiathar, "This is what Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders, and this is what I advised. **16** Now send word to David immediately: 'Don't camp at the river crossings in the wilderness tonight — cross over at once, or the king and everyone with him will be destroyed.'"

**17** Jonathan and Ahimaaz were stationed at En-rogel, since they couldn't risk being seen in the city. A servant girl would go out and pass messages to them, and they would carry the news to King David. **18** But a young man spotted them and reported it to Absalom. So the two of them hurried off and came to the house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard. They climbed down into it. **19** The man's wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, then scattered grain on top. No one could tell anything was there.

**20** When Absalom's men arrived at the house, they demanded, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman told them, "They crossed over the stream." The soldiers searched but found nothing, and went back to Jerusalem.

**21** After they had gone, the two men climbed out of the well and hurried to King David. "Get up and cross the river immediately!" they told him. "Ahithophel has advised them to attack you."

**22** David and all his people set out at once and crossed the Jordan. By dawn, every last person had made it across.

**23** When Ahithophel realized his advice had been rejected, he saddled his donkey and rode home to his own city. He put his affairs in order, then hanged himself. He died and was buried in his father's tomb.

**24** David arrived at Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.

**25** Absalom had appointed Amasa as army commander in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had married Abigail the daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

**26** Israel and Absalom set up camp in the land of Gilead.

**27** When David arrived at Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from the Ammonite city of Rabbah, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim **28** brought beds, bowls, pottery, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, **29** honey, butter, sheep, and cheese for David and his people. They said, "The people must be hungry and exhausted and parched out there in the wilderness."

---
*— PNEUMA*
